ui.title: Syntax guide
ui.subtitle: MEditor uses standard Markdown plus a few custom pieces of syntax. Every example below comes with its code and with what the app actually renders from it.
ui.onPaper: Printing starts a new page here

items: Standard syntax: CommonMark plus GFM (tables, strikethrough, task lists). Code blocks are highlighted when you name the language.
Custom syntax always looks the same: a block opens with `:::name` and closes with `:::`, and a one-line form is written `::name`.
Most of it can be inserted with a button on the toolbar.
Mermaid, LaTeX, charts and to-do lists are built-in plugins you can switch off in Settings → Plugins. Callouts and page breaks are core and always on.
A mistake never breaks the document: the preview shows the error in place.

blocks.text: There are two ways to write one. Form A uses a Markdown table as the data and is the everyday choice. Form B is a Chart.js configuration, for when you need fine control.
Wrap a table in `:::chart{…}` and close it with `:::`. The first column is the label and every other column is a data series.

blocks.alt: A bar chart made from a table, with two series for 2025 and 2026

head: Attribute
Meaning
rows: Kind of chart: `bar`, `line`, `area`, `pie`, `doughnut`, `radar` or `scatter`. Defaults to `bar`
Stack the series. Only for `bar` and `line`. Write it as `{type=bar stacked}`
Write `legend=false` to hide the legend. It shows by default when there are several series, or for pie charts

blocks.text: For `scatter`, the first column must be the numeric x value.
A code block whose language is `chart`, holding a Chart.js configuration in YAML or JSON. It needs `type` and `data`, and may add `width` and `height` in pixels.

blocks.alt: A line chart drawn from a Chart.js configuration, with Sales and Costs lines

items: YAML cannot hold functions, such as a tooltip callback.
Series without a colour get the theme's palette. A theme can change it with the CSS variables `--chart-1` to `--chart-8`.
A bad configuration shows a red error where the chart would be.

blocks.text: Write `[ ]` for open and `[x]` for done; capital `X` works too. There are three places to put one: on a line of its own, in a list (which can be nested), and in a table cell.

blocks.alt: The three ways to write to-dos: standalone lines, a nested list and table cells

items: Standalone lines and table cells need a space after the bracket; a cell holding only `[x]` does not.
In a list it is the standard `- [x]` form (a Markdown feature of its own), so it keeps working even when the to-do plugin is off.
Only a mark at the very start of a line is converted. A `[x]` in the middle of a sentence, or inside inline code, is left alone.
The checkboxes in the preview and in exports are read-only. To change one, edit the text.

blocks.text: Write a diagram in a code block whose language is `mermaid`. Flowcharts, sequence diagrams, Gantt charts and every other kind Mermaid supports work.

blocks.alt: A flowchart drawn from Mermaid code

items: A theme can restyle diagrams with CSS variables that start with `--mermaid-`, such as `--mermaid-line` and `--mermaid-font`.
A syntax error shows as a red message in the preview.

blocks.text: Wrap an inline formula in a single `$`, and put a display formula between two lines of `$$`. It uses KaTeX syntax.

blocks.alt: An inline formula and an integral on its own line

items: To show a literal dollar sign write `\$` (for example `\$5`); otherwise whatever lies between two `$` is read as a formula.
A `$` inside a code block or inline code is left alone.
A formula with a mistake is shown in red.

blocks.text: Wrap content in `:::note` or `:::warning` and close it with `:::`. Anything Markdown can do works inside.

blocks.alt: A note callout and a warning callout with its own title

items: Use `{title="…"}` to change the heading. By default it is note or warning.
**The outer block needs more colons than any block inside it**, or the inner closing `:::` closes the outer one too. To put a chart in a callout, open it with `::::note` and close it with `::::`.
A block with a name that is not recognised is shown as a plain block, not as an error.

blocks.text: Write `::pagebreak` on a line of its own. When you print or export to PDF, what follows starts on a new page.

items: It must be alone on its line.
It is not visible in the preview or on screen; it only breaks the page when printing.
An exported HTML file breaks the page the same way when it is printed from a browser.

blocks.text: An image on a line of its own, with description text, shows that text under the picture as a caption.

items: An image in the middle of a sentence, or one without description text, has no caption.
To hide captions, add `figcaption { display: none }` to the theme's CSS.
The toolbar's image button lets you drop several images in at once; the description is left empty, so add a caption only where you want one.
